intro: A verse of the Qur'an can be short, but the books written about it can fill a shelf. Muslims call this work of explaining the Qur'an tafsir. For more than a thousand years, scholars have asked what each verse means, why it came, and how it fits the rest of the book. They used grammar, reports about the Prophet, the history of the first Muslims, philosophy and the inner life of the soul. They often reached different answers, and they kept those answers side by side on the page.

In the last two centuries, the questions changed. Printing presses, colonial rule, modern science, new universities and the internet all reached Muslim readers. Reformers in Cairo, thinkers in South Asia, women scholars in the United States and translators in English all asked how an old text speaks to a new world. Muslims today disagree about many of these readings, and they discuss them in mosques, classrooms and online.

By the end of this unit you will be able to name the major classical commentators and describe their methods. You will compare how several readers explain the same verse. You will also describe the main modern approaches and the debates around them, and attribute every reading to the reader who holds it.
bigQuestion: How have Muslim readers, classical and modern, decided what the Qur'an means, and why do their readings differ?

timeline.t: Al-Tabari dies in Baghdad, leaving his vast commentary on the Qur'an
Al-Qushayri, a Sufi scholar, dies after writing a commentary on inner meanings
Al-Zamakhshari dies; his commentary the Kashshaf is known for its grammar
Al-Tabrisi, a Shia commentator, dies after completing his tafsir
Fakhr al-Din al-Razi dies; his large commentary joins philosophy to tafsir
Ibn Kathir dies; his tafsir explains the Qur'an by the Qur'an and hadith
Muhammad Abduh dies; Rashid Rida carries on their commentary, al-Manar
Marmaduke Pickthall publishes his English translation of the Qur'an
Sayyid Qutb is executed in Egypt; his commentary In the Shade of the Qur'an is widely read
Fazlur Rahman's Islam and Modernity describes his 'double movement' way of reading
Amina Wadud publishes Qur'an and Woman in Malaysia
Amina Wadud leads a mixed Friday prayer in New York, sparking wide debate

words.d: explanation or commentary on the Qur'an; also a book of such commentary
a scholar who writes tafsir, a commentator on the Qur'an
the occasions of revelation: reports about the events when, according to Muslim tradition, a verse came
abrogation: the view that a later ruling replaces an earlier one; scholars disagree about how often it applies
a clear verse whose meaning is settled, as described in Qur'an 3:7
an ambiguous or allegorical verse, open to more than one reading, as described in Qur'an 3:7
the chain of people who passed on a report, used to judge whether it is reliable
interpretation that looks beyond the plain sense; Sufi and philosophical readers use it for inner meanings
careful independent reasoning by a scholar to reach a judgment
Fazlur Rahman's method: move from a verse to the principle behind it in its first setting, then back to the present
reading verses as pointing to modern scientific findings; many scholars criticize the approach
a rendering of the Qur'an's meaning in another language; many Muslims hold that only the Arabic is the Qur'an itself

test.q: What does the word tafsir mean?
choices: The rules for reciting the Qur'an aloud
Explanation or commentary on the Qur'an
One of thirty equal parts of the Qur'an
A person who has memorized the Qur'an
test.why: Tafsir is commentary on the Qur'an. Reciting rules are tajwid, a thirtieth part is a juz', and a memorizer is a hafiz.

test.q: Al-Tabari's commentary is best known for which method?
choices: Collecting reports from earlier authorities with their chains, then choosing among them
Reading every verse as a symbol of the Sufi path
Linking verses to modern scientific discoveries
Explaining verses only by Shia imams' sayings
test.why: Al-Tabari gathered many reports with their isnads and then stated which reading he judged strongest.

test.q: Al-Zamakhshari's Kashshaf is especially valued for its attention to what?
test.why: Readers of many views used the Kashshaf for its grammar and rhetoric, even when they disagreed with its Mu'tazili theology.

test.q: Qur'an 3:7 divides the Book's verses into which two kinds?
test.why: Surah Al Imran 3:7 speaks of clear verses that are the foundation of the Book and others that are ambiguous.

test.q: A Sufi commentator such as al-Qushayri mainly looks for what in a verse?
choices: Its inner or spiritual meaning for the soul
Its date according to carbon testing
Its place in a modern constitution
test.why: Sufi tafsir reads for inner meanings, usually alongside the outer sense rather than instead of it.

test.q: Which commentator is known for explaining the Qur'an first by other verses of the Qur'an, then by hadith?
test.why: Ibn Kathir's tafsir follows the method of explaining the Qur'an by the Qur'an, then by hadith and early reports.

test.q: Al-Tabrisi is an important commentator in which tradition?
test.why: Al-Tabrisi wrote a major Shia (Twelver) tafsir, Majma' al-Bayan.

choices: Reports about the events when a verse came
test.why: Asbab al-nuzul are the occasions of revelation, used to read a verse in its setting.

test.q: Fazlur Rahman's 'double movement' asks a reader to do what?
choices: Move from a verse to its principle in its first setting, then apply that principle today
Compare Arabic with two English translations
test.why: Rahman described moving from the verse's historical setting to its general principle, and back to the present.

test.q: Muhammad Abduh and Rashid Rida are linked with which commentary?
choices: In the Shade of the Qur'an
test.why: Tafsir al-Manar began from Abduh's lessons and was written up and continued by Rida.

test.q: Amina Wadud's Qur'an and Woman argues what, as she presents it?
choices: That only men may read tafsir
That the Qur'an, read as a whole, affirms the equal worth of women and men
That the Qur'an should be read only in English
That tafsir should stop after the classical period
test.why: Wadud reads the Qur'an as a whole to argue for equality; other scholars disagree with some of her conclusions.

test.q: Why do many scholars criticize 'scientific exegesis'?
choices: They say it ties the text to theories that may change
They say the Qur'an has no verses about nature
They say it was invented by al-Tabari
test.why: Critics argue that linking verses to current science ties the text to theories that may later be revised.

test.q: Why can this course quote Pickthall's translation but not Yusuf Ali's or Arberry's?
choices: Pickthall's 1930 translation is in the public domain in the United States; the others are not
Pickthall's is the only accurate one
The others are not in English
test.why: It is a copyright question, not a verdict on quality: Pickthall (1930) entered the U.S. public domain in 2026.

test.q: Many Muslims call an English Qur'an 'the meaning of the Qur'an' because they hold what?
choices: That only the Arabic text is the Qur'an itself
That English is a holy language
That the Qur'an was first written in English
test.why: Many Muslims hold that a translation carries the meaning but is not the Qur'an itself; Pickthall's title reflects this.

test.q: In classical tafsir, what is naskh?
choices: The belief that a later ruling can replace an earlier one
test.why: Naskh, or abrogation, is the view that some later rulings replace earlier ones; scholars debate how many cases exist.

write.prompt: Choose one verse studied in this unit, such as Qur'an 3:7 (Al Imran), 24:35 (al-Nur) or 4:34 (al-Nisa'). How have at least one classical and one modern reader explained it? Cite the verse by surah and ayah, name each commentator and their method, explain what the verse says and how each reader reads it, and describe why their readings differ.
tips: Name the surah, the ayah and the translation you use.
Attribute every reading to the scholar who holds it.
Describe each method fairly before you compare.
Compare readings; do not rank them or judge the text.
Use the unit's terms, such as tafsir, asbab al-nuzul and muhkam.
